elements.problem: 'organophosphate poisoning likely' is encoded as Poisoning AND (ANY ONE of the signs). The page lists a cholinergic cluster; with a single-sign 'or', any poisoning/overdose patient with vomiting alone, diarrhoea alone, sweating alone, pulse < 60 alone or diastolic < 60 alone (e.g. paracetamol overdose with vomiting) becomes probable organophosphate poisoning. Logic should follow the page's cluster (and/any2, anchored on pinpoint pupils/secretions), and excessive secretions is missing. BP < 90/60 split into SBP<90 or DBP<60 is acceptable.

rule_level_problems.problem: Single-sign 'or' under Poisoning makes any poisoning with vomiting, diarrhoea, sweating, bradycardia or low diastolic BP a probable organophosphate poisoning; the page describes a cholinergic cluster. Excessive secretions omitted.

'Shock¹' relies on a directly recorded Shock disorder; footnote 1's shock-likely criteria (SBP<80, pulse>=100, RR>30, confusion/restlessness, weakness) are not encoded as a probable Shock rule feeding (active_condition Shock), as the house standard asks.
Non-urgent flowchart branch 'Toxic dose -> Refer urgently' not encoded; arguably not representable.
Agitation coded as Feeling agitated (emotional state) rather than Psychomotor agitation; general weakness coded as Muscle weakness.

summary: The red box is encoded faithfully as an Urgent priority rule on Poisoning (which overdose descends from), with every criterion present. The most consequential problem is the organophosphate rule: it fires on any single cholinergic sign (e.g. vomiting alone in any poisoning), and excessive secretions is missing. Footnote 1's 'shock likely' has no probable Shock rule, so the red-box 'Shock' item only fires on a directly recorded Shock.
